title: ‘We cannot hold peace talks at gunpoint’: Security build-up deepens distrust over dam

ai.summary: Protests against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project dam in Arunachal Pradesh have escalated with violence, arrests, and heavy security deployment since September 2024, with demands for the release of detained protesters before peace talks.

facts.claim: Protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) dam in Arunachal Pradesh have escalated into violence, arrests and a heavy security deployment.
facts.quote: Protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) dam in Arunachal Pradesh have escalated into violence, arrests and a heavy security deployment.

facts.claim: Hundreds of police personnel and paramilitary forces were deployed to the region since September 14, when residents called for a halt to all pre-feasibility studies (PFR) towards the SUMP – a massive hydroelectric and flood-control dam projected to generate roughly 11,200 MW of power.
facts.quote: Hundreds of police personnel and paramilitary forces were deployed to the region since September 14, when residents called for a halt to all pre-feasibility studies (PFR) towards the SUMP – a massive hydroelectric and flood-control dam projected to generate roughly 11,200 MW of power.

facts.claim: In early October, tensions escalated when four protesters were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014.
facts.quote: In early October, tensions escalated when four protesters were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014.

facts.claim: The police has filed at least eight cases and arrested 26 people in connection to the violence.
facts.quote: The police has filed at least eight cases and arrested 26 people in connection to the violence.

facts.claim: A central demand from residents and agitating groups is the release of those detained by the police.
